title: Reconcile received items from receipts before changing inventory (provider-neutral)
body:
## Role
A backend engineer building provider-neutral reconciliation.

## Goal
Let the household record what actually arrived (backlog P2.3), starting with manual receipt upload, so inventory changes only from confirmed evidence.

## Context
The Instacart Developer Platform pages read document no order, cart or receipt access, so reconciliation can't come from the adapter. #117 and #97 were symptoms of the old design, where ordering itself marked inventory restocked.

## Deliverables
- Manual receipt entry or upload producing proposed observations (#134) for matched HouseholdItems (#133).
- Review step for ambiguous or substituted items.
- Received state applied only after confirmation.
- A link from a fulfillment attempt to its reconciliation, when the user makes one.

## Concrete examples
- A receipt lists "Organic Carrots 2 lb"; the plan had carrots; the user confirms; carrots become `on_hand` with source `receipt`.
- A receipt lists an unknown item; it waits in review and changes nothing.

## Constraints
- Provider-neutral: no Instacart import unless #139 finds an authorized source.
- A handoff attempt alone never changes inventory.

## Dependencies
#133, #134, #143.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Ordered, substituted, refunded and received are distinguishable.
- [ ] A test proves a `created` handoff without a confirmed receipt leaves inventory unchanged.

## Testing requirements
Unit and API tests with fixture receipts; no model calls in normal runs.

## Out of scope
Email forwarding, OCR quality work, provider order import.

## Documentation requirements
Backlog P2.3 marked in progress; README describes manual reconciliation.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
